title: How Much Does LASIK Cost in Barcelona? 2026 Price Guide
description: Typical 2026 LASIK prices in Barcelona and Spain per eye, what different laser types cost, what is included, and how to compare clinics safely.

segments.text: Laser eye surgery is one of the most price-compared treatments in Spain, and headline prices look very different from clinic to clinic. What matters is what is included, which laser technology is used and who performs the procedure. This guide covers typical 2026 prices and what to check before you commit.

content.text: How much does LASIK cost in Barcelona in 2026?

segments.text: LASIK typically costs about €800 to €2,500 per eye in Spain in 2026, with some high-end clinics charging up to €3,000, according to one published guide updated in June 2026. Two Barcelona clinics advertise all-inclusive LASIK from about €990 per eye and from about €1,100 per eye, while a premium hospital-based package is listed in dollars at roughly $3,300 to $4,500 for both eyes.

items: Traditional LASIK: roughly €800 to €1,500 per eye.
Wavefront or topography-guided LASIK, which customise the treatment: roughly €1,500 to €2,500 per eye.
SMILE, a minimally invasive alternative: roughly €2,000 to €3,000 per eye.
Both eyes: usually double the per-eye price, though some clinics offer package discounts.

content.text: What should be included in the price?

segments.text: Some clinics quote an all-inclusive price covering the consultation, procedure and aftercare, and others charge each item separately. One Barcelona clinic lists an all-in price with the pre-operative assessment, surgeon and anaesthetist fees, follow-up visits and cover for complications for a year. Another starts at a lower base price, with follow-up visits for three months and retreatment within six months included, and charges separately for eye drops of roughly €30 to €50.

segments.text: Often yes. Several clinics offer a free first informational visit, though the full pre-operative assessment with diagnostic tests may be charged separately or included in the package. Ask exactly what the free visit covers, because the assessment decides whether you are suitable for LASIK at all.

No. Suitability depends on your prescription, corneal thickness and eye health, and a properly qualified ophthalmologist decides this after tests. A clinic that promises suitability without a full assessment should be treated with caution. This guide is general information and not medical advice, and LASIK, like all surgery, carries risks that your surgeon should explain.

content.text: How can I compare clinics fairly?

items: Get the price in writing for the exact technology and both eyes.
Ask which laser platform is used and who operates.
Compare the aftercare period and the retreatment terms.
Ask about financing, since interest-free instalments are common.
Take your time, and get a second assessment if you are unsure.

content.text: What is the difference between the laser types?

segments.text: Traditional LASIK uses a blade to create the corneal flap, while femto-LASIK uses a laser for the flap and is generally priced higher. Wavefront and topography-guided treatments customise the correction to the shape of your eye, and SMILE is a minimally invasive alternative. Which is suitable depends on your eyes, and a good clinic will explain why it recommends one option over another rather than simply the most expensive.

Clinics describe LASIK as an outpatient procedure that takes about 15 to 20 minutes per eye, with most people back to normal activity within a day or two, followed by aftercare visits over the following weeks and months. Individual recovery varies, and your surgeon will give instructions on eye drops, rest and follow-up appointments. Ask about the plan for any complications before you agree to treatment.

Do not choose on price alone. A lower price can be entirely legitimate, but it should never mean a shorter assessment or a rushed decision. Ask to meet the surgeon before the day, ask how many procedures the clinic performs and take the written consent form home to read in your own time. If anything is unclear in English, ask for it to be explained until it is.
Prices change, so confirm the current figure with the clinic.

faqs.q: How much does LASIK cost in Barcelona?
faqs.a: Roughly €800 to €2,500 per eye in Spain in 2026, with some Barcelona clinics advertising all-inclusive prices from about €990 to €1,100 per eye.

faqs.q: Is LASIK cheaper in Spain than in the UK or US?
faqs.a: Published comparisons suggest Spain is often competitive, but prices vary by clinic and technology, so compare what is included.

faqs.q: What is included in the price of LASIK?
faqs.a: It varies. Some clinics include assessment, surgery, aftercare and retreatment, while others charge each separately and add eye drops.

faqs.q: Is the first LASIK consultation free in Barcelona?
faqs.a: Often. Several clinics offer a free informational visit, but the full pre-operative assessment may be charged separately.
